verdict: TJX sales rose 5% to $15.2B with every division growing, and a $219M net benefit from tariff refunds helped lift EPS 24% to $1.36.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net sales of $15.2B vs $14.4B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: up 24% YoY; adjusted EPS $1.22 excluding the tariff-refund benefit

kpis.label: Comparable sales
kpis.note: above plan; HomeGoods, Canada and International each up 6–7%

kpis.label: Pretax margin
kpis.note: includes 1.4 points from tariff refunds; adjusted margin 11.9%

segments.name: Marmaxx (U.S.)
segments.note: T.J. Maxx, Marshalls and Sierra stores in the U.S. — the biggest division, though its 1% comparable-sales gain lagged the rest.

segments.name: HomeGoods (U.S.)
segments.note: HomeGoods and Homesense home-fashions stores in the U.S. — comparable sales up 7%.

segments.name: TJX International
segments.note: TK Maxx and Homesense in Europe and Australia — the fastest-growing division, with comparable sales up 7%.

segments.name: TJX Canada
segments.note: Winners, HomeSense and Marshalls in Canada — comparable sales up 6%.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative — store wages and payroll, rent-related running costs not in cost of sales, marketing and the back office. Includes extra bonus accruals linked to the tariff refunds.

otherDetail: Net interest income of $31M — interest earned on cash slightly exceeded interest costs.
oneTimers: Tariff refunds gave TJX a $219M net pretax benefit this quarter ($0.14 per share): refunds received, minus $112M of extra year-end bonus accruals the windfall triggered. Excluding it, adjusted EPS was $1.22 (up 11%) and adjusted pretax margin was 11.9% instead of 13.3%. More refunds are expected in Q3, in uncertain amounts.
footerNote: TJX had not yet reported Q3 FY27 as of November 7, 2026 (that quarter ended October 31, 2026), so this page covers its latest reported quarter, Q2 FY27.

takeaways.title: Growth everywhere except the flagship
takeaways.text: Consolidated comparable sales rose 4%, above plan — but Marmaxx (T.J. Maxx/Marshalls U.S.) managed only +1%, while HomeGoods, Canada and International each rose 6–7%.

takeaways.title: Refunds padded the profit beat
takeaways.text: EPS of $1.36 includes a $0.14 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. The adjusted figure, $1.22, was still up 11% — and TJX raised its full-year outlook on the strength of the quarter.

takeaways.title: A bigger long-term map
takeaways.text: TJX lifted its long-term store target to 7,500 stores and plans to speed openings to 4% a year from FY28 — it ended the quarter with 5,285 stores.
